paper.central_claim: A five-agent framework (Actor, Critic, Insight, Skill, Online) with a self-evolving Skillhub automates end-to-end system-level configuration optimization of multi-stage recommenders via live A/B tests and continuously self-improves, as shown by multiple successful production launches on Google Discover.
paper.title: AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; null by contract.

evidence.quote: The effectiveness of AgenticRecTune is demonstrated by multiple successful production launches on Google Discover.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim is launch-based; no numbers in the abstract.

evidence.quote: Any structural modification to the underlying models, including a change in feature engineering or a shift in model architecture, invalidates previous settings and necessitates a global recalibration of system-level parameters.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: system-level config (fusion weights, thresholds) must be retuned after every model change; asserted, no cost numbers.

evidence.quote: Despite these advancements, existing approaches remain confined to offline preprocessing (feature mining) or model-level structural mutations (editing network layers).
evidence.support_explanation: Author positioning against Self-EvolveRec / AgenticTagger / YouTube MLE agents: system-level online orchestration is the claimed residue.

evidence.quote: The Skill Agent then identifies patterns relevant to specific skills and automatically appends these refined rules to the Domain Knowledge component of that skill.
evidence.support_explanation: Skill update = append LLM-extracted rules to a skill's Domain Knowledge; no stated validation of an appended rule.

evidence.quote: Simultaneously, it dynamically tightens the search space bounds within the Task Requirements.
evidence.support_explanation: Persistent change to allowed value ranges; premature exclusion risk and rollback not discussed.

evidence.quote: Before online A/B testing starts, the users’ review is required.
evidence.support_explanation: Human gate before every online test; autonomy claim ('no longer requires human effort') is qualified.

evidence.quote: It filters out suboptimal configurations, selects the most promising candidates for deployment, and provides detailed feedback comments.
evidence.support_explanation: Critic is an LLM filter on proposals before the (real) A/B evaluation.

evidence.quote: The system maintains a "top performers" pool by systematically discarding candidates that are strictly outperformed by others.
evidence.support_explanation: Pareto-elite retention rule in Agent Memory; read by Actor in next prompt.

evidence.quote: Crucially, this empirical performance data is then written back into the Agent Memory by updating the corresponding JSON files.
evidence.support_explanation: Execution feedback persisted and re-read; the closed loop on configs/memory is real.

evidence.quote: Live user traffic was randomly partitioned into orthogonal buckets.
evidence.support_explanation: Randomized online A/B against production control gives a credible measurement channel.

evidence.quote: Each experiment was run as a standard launch period to ensure statistical significance (evaluated at a p-value < 0.05).
evidence.support_explanation: Only statistical statement; no per-row p-values, intervals, traffic share, or multiple-comparison handling across the candidate arms.

evidence.quote: Value-Based Retrieval Pre-Ranking 0.75% 0.90% 0.48%
evidence.support_explanation: Relative lifts on anonymized metrics (Engagement 1/2, Diversity); no baselines or absolute values.

evidence.quote: Diversity Re-Ranking 0.21% 0.29% 3.43%
evidence.support_explanation: Same row reappears as the Gemini 3 Pro row of Table 2, so ablations are single A/B reruns of one reported result.

evidence.quote: Single Agent Strategy 0.29% 0.26% 0.06%
evidence.support_explanation: Actor-only baseline for Actor-Critic ablation; single A/B each, no variance.

evidence.quote: Pro models (Gemini 3 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Pro) have better performance compared with Flash model under the Diversity task in the re-ranking stage.
evidence.support_explanation: Caption says re-ranking, while Sec 5.3 says the diversity task in the pre-ranking stage: internal inconsistency in the ablation setting.

evidence.quote: The Actor-Critic configuration achieved a 0.75% and 0.90% lift in engagement metric 1 and 2, respectively, which is more than double than the gains observed with the Actor-only agent.
evidence.support_explanation: Only controlled ablation of an agent component; round counts and A/B budgets are not stated.

evidence.quote: Finally, the Insight Agent detects sensitive parameters with the highest impact across iterations and extracts patterns of primary metrics from individual tasks to inform future optimizations.
evidence.support_explanation: Insight agent distills outcomes into patterns that feed the Skillhub; extraction is LLM-based over a small number of A/B outcomes with no credit assignment described.

evidence.quote: AgenticRecTune leverages its reasoning loop and vast amounts of historical data to explore this high-dimensional weight space significantly more efficiently than traditional grid search methods.
evidence.support_explanation: Efficiency claim vs grid search/human tuning asserted without a comparison or cost figures.

evidence.quote: We observed that AgenticRecTune provides novel insights into configuration tuning, identifying impactful parameter interactions that engineers had previously missed.
evidence.support_explanation: Anecdotal; the learned patterns are not shown.

evidence.quote: This allows the system to develop sophisticated tuning strategies without requiring human intervention to manually author new skill definitions.
evidence.support_explanation: Novel-skill generation claim; text says it mainly updates the domain-knowledge section, with no example or evaluation.

evidence.quote: Zhang et al. (2025) introduce Agentic Context Engineering (ACE), a multi-agent framework that conceptualizes contexts as dynamic playbooks.
evidence.support_explanation: Closest evolving-context neighbour is mentioned in one sentence and not compared.

evidence.quote: After rounds of small traffic of iteration, AgenticRecTune succesfully search the better candidate compared with baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection happens over several small-traffic rounds; whether reported Table 1 numbers come from fresh traffic for the selected arm is not stated.

evidence.quote: It no longer requires human effort anymore and overcomes the scalability limitations of manually driven iterations.
evidence.support_explanation: Overstated against E006 (user review before each A/B).

gap.author_gap: System-level configuration tuning (non-differentiable glue of the multi-stage recommender) is costly, needs cross-stage expertise and must be redone after every model change; prior LLM/ML-agent work is offline or model-level.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and industrially relevant, but evidence of cost is asserted, and the obvious classical neighbours (Bayesian/bandit online parameter tuning, grid search, human tuning) are not compared. The distinct part vs generic LLM-as-optimizer is the Skillhub.
gap.lineage: AutoML/HPO -> LLM HPO agents (AgentHPO) and autoresearch -> ML-engineering agents (AI Scientist, PACEvolve) -> recsys-specific agents (AgenticTagger, Self-EvolveRec, YouTube MLE) ; evolving context playbooks (ACE).
gap.closest_adjacent: ACE-style evolving playbooks and recsys self-evolving agents; these solve offline/model-level or generic context evolution, per the authors.
gap.residue: Online, multi-metric, noisy, delayed-feedback optimization of fusion/threshold configs by an LLM loop that learns reusable tuning knowledge.
gap.stakes: Engineering effort per model change; production metrics. No quantified baseline effort.
gap.method_response: LLM proposals + online A/B oracle + memory/insight distillation into a skill store.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether the Skillhub evolution (versus plain LLM search with memory) contributes; cost per launch; robustness of learned rules under distribution shift.
gap.unresolved: Comparison with classical online optimizers; value of self-evolving Skillhub.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: LLM-proposed configurations selected through live A/B rounds beat the production control at three stages (stat. sig. at 0.05), and in one task Actor-Critic beat Actor-only. The evidence does not show that the persisted Skillhub/memory caused gains (no store-off arm), so level stays task.
assessment.unresolved: Skillhub contribution; selection vs reporting traffic; run-to-run variance; cost; comparison with classical tuners; retained improvement over successive model versions.

G.reason: Real, specific non-weight object (fusion weights/thresholds that must be re-tuned per model change) with cited recsys-agent neighbours, but cost is asserted not measured, classical Bayesian/bandit online tuners are not treated as neighbours, and ACE-style evolving contexts get one sentence.

M.reason: Loop (propose, critique, real A/B, memory, insight, skill) is reconstructable and the A/B oracle fits the problem; why LLM+skills should beat BO/bandits and how appended rules are expected to generalize is not argued, and skill-update logic is vague.

X.reason: Memory schema, Pareto pruning, diversity selection and next-prompt reading are described; skill updates (append rules, tighten bounds) have no admission gate, versioning, rollback, expiry or conflict handling, no learned-rule examples, and a human review step contradicts the autonomy narrative.

E.measurement.reason: Randomized live production A/B is a credible measurement channel, but metrics are anonymized relative lifts with no absolute values or per-row significance, the Table 2 setting is inconsistently labeled, and multi-arm selection effects are not handled.

E.causality.reason: Only Actor-Critic-vs-Actor and LLM-size comparisons exist (single runs). The central self-evolving Skillhub/memory/Insight claim has no on/off arm and no tuner baseline for the efficiency claim; reasonable for a deployment note but weak against the stated claims.

E.holdout.reason: Live traffic buckets give a real outcome channel, but selection rounds and reported lifts are not separated, ablations reuse reported results, and cross-system transfer is absent.

E.statistics.reason: A blanket p<0.05 statement for A/B tests, but no sample sizes, intervals, per-row tests, agent-run variance or multiple-comparison control; single run per ablation.

E.cost.reason: Efficiency and scalability are claimed, yet no LLM calls, number of A/B rounds, traffic share, wall-clock or human review time is given.

rationale: A/B 闭环与记忆/Skillhub 持久化真实存在，线上有显著提升；但自演化 Skillhub 无关闭对照，成本未报，选择与报告流量未分，证据仅 task 级。
